rules.title: LA JCO: no termination of tenancy without just cause
rules.requirement: For covered Los Angeles rental units, a landlord may not terminate a tenancy without just cause. The page lists at-fault reasons (e.g., failure to pay rent, nuisance, illegal use) and no-fault reasons (e.g., owner or family move-in, demolition, government order) as legal reasons for eviction.
rules.citation: Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO), per LAHD webpage
rules.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.
rules.exemptions: Page says the JCO covers most residential properties not regulated by the RSO. Exceptions include, but are not limited to, transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, an owner's roommate, certain cooperatives, some non-profit homeless facilities or short-term substance abuse treatment centers, and some HACLA or government-owned properties. The JCO applies to a tenancy only once the tenant has lived in the unit at least six months or the original lease has expired, whichever comes first.
rules.interaction: The page states the JCO does not regulate rent increases. Units subject to the City's Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) are outside the JCO's coverage as described on the page.

rules.title: LA JCO: relocation assistance for no-fault evictions
rules.requirement: For covered Los Angeles rental units, a landlord must provide relocation assistance to the tenant when the eviction is no-fault (e.g., owner or immediate family move-in, demolition or removal from the rental market). At-fault tenants are not entitled to relocation assistance.
rules.citation: Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO), per LAHD webpage
rules.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.
rules.exemptions: Same JCO exceptions as the termination rule (transient hotels, licensed care facilities, etc.). The page says an owner "may have to pay" relocation assistance and gives no amounts or per-reason conditions.
rules.interaction: Relocation amounts and per-reason conditions are not stated in this source and need review against the ordinance text.

rules.title: LA: no nonpayment eviction unless rent owed exceeds Fair Market Rent
rules.requirement: For all RSO and JCO rental units in Los Angeles, a landlord may not evict a tenant for falling behind in rent unless the amount owed is higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR) for the unit's bedroom size.
rules.citation: Los Angeles JCO/RSO nonpayment eviction provision (effective March 27, 2023), per LAHD webpage
rules.quoted_span: Effective March 27, 2023, landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes an amount higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR).
rules.key_value: Rent owed must exceed the Fair Market Rent for the unit's bedroom size
rules.exemptions: Not stated beyond the underlying RSO and JCO coverage limits.
rules.interaction: The page applies this to all RSO and JCO units. It gives no FMR dollar amounts.
